body.p: The following concepts are central to understanding how Content Fusion works.

section.title: Organizations
section.p: As a cloud service, separates collaboration workspaces into Organizations. An Organization is the central container for users, projects, and resources. As a platform user, you can either create a new Organization and become its admin, or join an existing Organization and become a member of that Organization. All content collaboration and project work takes place within the context of an Organization.

section.title: Projects
section.p: The Project is the main module for managing your content. A project typically connects to a Git repository that stores the project files, such as DITA topics, maps, images, and other supporting resources. Within a project, users can browse and manage files, edit content in the web editor, commit changes to the repository, create and manage review tasks, define publications and generate deliverables.

section.title: Repository
section.p: A Repository is a Git repository for a project. The repository is used to maintain the history of revisions, and allows teams to track and manage changes.

section.title: Personal Workspace
section.p: The Personal Workspace is your private working area within a project. It functions as a personal working copy of the repository, allowing you to modify multiple files without immediately affecting the shared project content. Changes made in the Personal Workspace remain private until you commit them, at which point they become visible to other project members in the shared repository.

section.title: Review Tasks
section.p: A Review Task allows authors to share content with reviewers for feedback. Within a review task, reviewers can read and navigate the content, add comments, suggest edits, participate in discussions with authors and other reviewers.

section.title: Publications
section.p: A Publication represents a logical documentation set within a project. It defines a specific collection of content that forms a complete documentation product, such as a user guide for a particular product, version, or audience. A publication is typically defined by a DITA map that organizes the content structure and a filter configuration (DITA profiling conditions) that selects the applicable content.

section.title: Deliverables
section.p: A Deliverable is the output generated from a publication using a publishing transformation.
